newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK democrats launch protest balloons into China.
newsitem.headline: HK democrats launch protest balloons into China.

text.p: Pro-democracy activists sent 50 helium-filled balloons attached to a banner drifting into China on Saturday in protest against Beijing's plan to scrap Hong Kong's elected legislature.
Members of the United Front Against the Provisional Legislature drove into a restricted area at the Lok Ma Chau border post to launch the balloons and banner.
The banner called on people to "oppose the provisional legislature". Police allowed the protest to take place but then asked the group to leave the area.

Group spokesman Andrew Cheng, a legislator from the Democratic Party, said members released the balloons because China would not let them travel over the border to Shenzhen where a Beijing-controlled 400-member Selection Committee was choosing the provisional legislature.
"We cannot go into the Shenzhen area to protest but our balloons -- our spirit of protest -- will continue to fight against such an anti-democratic body," Cheng said.

China plans to install the legislature upon taking the colony back from Britain at midnight on June 30 next year, and to disband the Legislative Council that was elected by over one million Hong Kong voters last year.
